source.title: Characterizing Datapoints via Second-Split Forgetting
source.authors: Pratyush Maini; S. Garg; Zachary Chase Lipton; J. Kolter

record.file_problem: none; full paper and supplementary material are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study removes examples ranked by second-split forgetting time and reports effects on test accuracy, a different selection method from the versions’ mapped interventions.
record.gate_note: The study reports its own example-removal results on CIFAR-10 test accuracy. It does not test any listed version’s specific behavior or measurement. Claims about other methods in the related work and comparisons to prior studies are cited results, not rows.
record.test_reason: The study measures example learning and forgetting dynamics and the utility of SSFT-based data removal. It does not test any listed version. In particular, neither SSFT nor first-split learning time measures V8's inclusion-dependent memorization score; removing examples selected by these metrics does not establish an effect of removing the most memorized examples.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors present SSFT as complementary to first-split learning metrics, useful for identifying mislabeled examples and diagnosing failure modes, and capable of improving generalization through removal of problematic examples. They also acknowledge sensitivity to the second-split learning rate.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses second-split forgetting time to rank examples for removal; it does not reproduce the claim versions’ methods or measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: SSFT-based removal gains differ between DCGAN and DDPM generated data; the reported generalization effect also differs between noisy and clean CIFAR-10 settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Removing low-SSFT examples improves CIFAR-10 test accuracy with noisy or synthetic training data; reported synthetic-data gains reach up to 10% for DCGAN and remain under 2% for DDPM. On clean data, removal is less harmful than random removal.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Removing quickly forgotten examples can improve generalization when training data contain problematic examples; effectiveness depends on data quality and the second split used for ranking.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 4.5 and Figure 4 report that removing examples with the highest first-split learning times harms test accuracy more than random removal on clean CIFAR-10. This selection does not directly measure inclusion-dependent memorization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Slowly learned training examples can contribute more to held-out accuracy than randomly selected examples.

record.problems: The test-accuracy results in Figure 4 are not numerically described in the text apart from the reported gains. No uncertainty estimates are stated for these results.
record.rows_left_out: No result rows omitted. The study’s optimizer comparisons concern separation of mislabeled samples by SSFT, not held-out generalization comparisons in V4.

untested.parts: Matched random-label and natural-label training, including held-out accuracy under each labeling.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected test performance and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD held-out performance under specified tuning budgets; optimizer comparisons here concern example separation.
Batch-size effects on held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Dropout interventions and their effects on held-out error.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, generalization gaps, and comparison with alternative generalization measures.
Retraining after removing examples ranked by inclusion-dependent memorization, compared with equally sized random removals.

record.verdict_notes: The T2 assignment is unsupported because the removal rankings measure different constructs from V8. States are cannot_determine relative to the listed versions; the reported SSFT-cleansing improvements themselves are supported by the text.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and generalization on natural labels.
Width sweeps past the interpolation threshold and test error.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relationship to the training-test gap.
The study removes examples ranked by SSFT, not examples selected by influence estimation as most memorized.

rows.subject: ResNet-9
rows.stage_stated: trained on synthetic CIFAR10-like data; pseudo-labels assigned using the BiT model
rows.operation_detail: Remove examples with the lowest SSFT, then measure accuracy on the CIFAR-10 test set.
rows.value: SSFT removal improves generalization by up to 10% on the clean test set; figure only
rows.note: The text reports the improvement, but the plotted values are figure-only.
rows.check: The reported improvement is an SSFT-cleansing result, not an effect named by a claim version. Add that SSFT uses a clean CIFAR-10 second split to rank synthetic examples. The text reports up to 10% accuracy improvement without specifying an exact comparison point against random removal.

rows.subject: ResNet-9
rows.stage_stated: trained on synthetic CIFAR10-like data; pseudo-labels assigned using the BiT model
rows.operation_detail: Remove examples with the lowest SSFT, then measure accuracy on the CIFAR-10 test set.
rows.value: Generalization gains are under 2%; figure only
rows.note: The text describes gains under 2%, smaller than for DCGAN-generated data.
rows.check: Gains under 2% concern SSFT cleansing and cannot be classified as partial evidence for any version. Add the clean CIFAR-10 second split used for ranking synthetic examples; the exact gain against random removal is not stated.

rows.subject: ResNet-9
rows.operation_detail: Remove examples with the lowest SSFT, then measure accuracy on the CIFAR-10 test set.
rows.value: Removing easily forgotten examples has a lower negative impact on generalization than removing random samples; figure only
rows.note: The authors describe a relative reduction in harm, not a stated numerical gain.
rows.check: Lower harm from removing low-SSFT examples does not measure removal of examples selected by V8's memorization score. The qualitative value is supported, but its partial state has no applicable version.

rows.subject: ResNet-9
rows.stage_stated: trained on CIFAR-10 with 10% label noise
rows.operation_detail: Remove examples with the lowest SSFT, then measure accuracy on the CIFAR-10 test set.
rows.value: Removing examples based on SSFT helps improve generalization; figure only
rows.note: The text explicitly says SSFT-based removal helps improve generalization in the presence of noisy examples.
rows.check: Improvement after removing low-SSFT examples from label-corrupted data is supported, but does not measure any listed version's effect.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
